entries.description: Immigration court backlog reaches record 1.7+ million cases with average wait times of nearly 900 days (almost 2.5 years)
entries.causation_evidence: EOIR January 2026 report and TRAC Immigration Court Backlog data
entries.update_note: SUPERSEDED IN SCALE, DISPUTED IN TREND -- see jud_harm_015. Sources disagree sharply on the current backlog figure (TRAC: ~3.2M as of June 2026; CIS.org: 'below 3.5M' as of Q2 FY26, down from 3.57M; other outlets cite 1.7-2M using different scope/definitions). Recommend lowering confidence on the original 1.7M figure to MEDIUM and treating it as a point-in-time snapshot rather than the current state.

entries.description: Major hack of federal courts' CM/ECF system exposes sealed documents including wiretaps and confidential informants; slow response to prior 2020 breach
entries.causation_evidence: Reuters/Politico reporting, Senate cybersecurity concerns, Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts public statement (Aug 7, 2025)
entries.update_note: DATE CORRECTION + REINFORCED. Judiciary became internally aware of the full severity around July 4, 2025, but the breach was not publicly confirmed until Aug 7-8, 2025. Judge Michael Scudder (Judicial Conference IT Committee chair) testified CM/ECF and PACER are outdated and unsustainable due to cyber risk and require full replacement, with only incremental rollout planned. As of the most recent reporting found, CM/ECF remains active and some districts have shifted to hand-filing sealed documents rather than replacing the system outright -- see new entry jud_harm_016.
